messages:
Tom (SE): kicking off thread — customer POC failing when calling PrivateLink endpoint from their on‑prem network. 502 / TLS handshake timeouts. customer says it worked from their dev laptop but fails from corporate-managed workstations.

Priya (AE): region? endpoint DNS? are they using interface endpoint (vpce) or NLB fronted private endpoint?

Tom (SE): eu-west-1, interface endpoint (vpce). Endpoint DNS: vpce-0a1b2c3d-redwood.private.redwood.ai. Repro steps (from corporate laptop behind proxy):
```
$ curl -v https://vpce-0a1b2c3d-redwood.private.redwood.ai/health
* Connected to proxy.company.com (10.10.10.2) port 3128 (#0)
* TLS handshake timeout
* Closing connection 0
curl: (28) Operation timed out after 30001 milliseconds with 0 out of 0 bytes received
```

Jules (SRE): can you paste an openssl s_client and a dig +trace from the failing workstation? also check whether the corporate proxy is doing TLS inspection (MITM). health checks on the NLB side can be picky if SNI is rewritten.

Tom (SE): dig +trace output (abridged):
```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> vpce-0a1b2c3d-redwood.private.redwood.ai +trace
;; global options: +cmd
;; Received 192.0.2.10
vpce-0a1b2c3d-redwood.private.redwood.ai. 300 IN A 10.0.5.23
```
openssl s_client -connect vpce-0a1b2c3d-redwood.private.redwood.ai:443 -servername vpce-0a1b2c3d-redwood.private.redwood.ai
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = *.redwood-inference.com
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
no peer certificate available
---
SSL_connect: error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
```

Chris (Sales Eng): that verify error + the curl behavior smells like a proxy doing TLS inspection and substituting certs (unknown CA). Many enterprise proxies also rewrite SNI (so the origin sees a different SNI). If the NLB or our routing relies on SNI for certificate selection / ALPN routing it can fail.

Tom (SE): found proxy logs showing outbound connection rewritten: `PROXY_SSL_INSPECT: replaced-sni=redwood-corp` and header `X-INSPECTED: true`. Customer confirmed they run a TLS inspection appliance for egress.

Jules (SRE): root cause likely TLS inspection on corporate egress + endpoint relying on client seeing original cert chain / SNI. Two options: 1) Add an explicit bypass / allowlist in the TLS inspection appliance for the vpce hostname (preferred for POC). 2) If they can't bypass, they need to install the proxy CA into their trust store across fleet (operationally heavy). Also validate NLB target group is set to TLS passthrough (no TLS termination differences).

Priya (AE): customer asked: "if we bypass proxy for the endpoint, does this change cost/architecture?" quick answer: no pricing delta for bypass — it's a network policy change on their side. If they opt to move to Dedicated or Private (full private deployment), that affects pricing — we can share numbers in the pricing doc. I linked the Private vs Dedicated one-pager in the funnel.

Tom (SE): confirmed workaround: security team added exception for `vpce-0a1b2c3d-redwood.private.redwood.ai` in the proxy, restarted agent, curl now succeeds: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` :thumbsup:

Jules (SRE): follow ups for the POC checklist: add a note to the runbook about "no TLS inspection for Redwood POC endpoints"; verify NLB target protocol is TLS passthrough and SNI not rewritten; check healthcheck path and headers. I'll update the internal POC playbook.

Priya (AE): security questionnaire item answered — we told them we require no TLS intercept for private endpoints during POC, added suggested language for their security team. Also offered to have solutions eng do a short 30m call with their infra team.

deploy-bot: created ticket REDWOOD-POC-3127 (private endpoint proxy bypass confirmed).

Tom (SE): thanks everyone — marking this thread resolved from POC blocker POV. will reopen if anything else pops up.
